routes.gap_parts: Reliability: hard328 share about .43 of the ~42-problem base-to-RL gap (about 18 right answers; .63-.67 on MATH-500), the problems where the model's modal value is right but single samples miss it; the vote recovers most of these, and the extra draws go only to problems whose first two answers split (the 2-2 ties of vote-over-4). Budget (about .27, ~11): kept rather than won, because the full 16,384 cap stays on every sample and no sample is shortened. Answer statement (~.03, ~1): partly, since a malformed final line rarely becomes the mode. Capability (about .27, ~11): not reachable, because the vote cannot exceed problems whose mode is right.
routes.why: Pretraining fixes each problem's distribution over final values and a vote converges to its mode, so the vote's ceiling is the set of modal-right problems and extra samples only resolve near-ties. Spending samples where the first two disagree, and stopping at a 3-vote majority, should give about vote-over-5 accuracy at roughly 3 samples' tokens.

routes.gap_parts: Reliability (about 0.43-0.63 of the gap; on hard328 about 15-20 of the 42-problem one-sample gap are problems the model solves in some samples): min-p plus the vote converts sometimes-solved problems to their right modal value with 3 samples instead of 4-8. Answer statement (about 0.03 of the gap, 1-2 problems): tail draws that garble the final line or drift into another script are cut. Budget (about 0.25, up to about 10 problems) is only partly touched: fewer drifting samples run to the cap. Capability (about 0.27 on hard328) is not won back: the vote cannot move a wrong mode.
routes.why: Pretraining (and SFT on top of it) fixes each problem's distribution over final values and a vote converges to its mode, with samples beyond about eight only resolving ties; cutting the low-probability tail with min-p moves each sample's draw toward that mode, so a 3-sample vote should reach nearly the 4-sample vote's ceiling at three quarters of its tokens.
